title: KV cache fair-share throttling and rebalance playbook for tenant burst storms
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
During a customer-facing capacity incident on 2025-02-07 we observed cascading cache miss storms that originated from a single tenant burst. The KV prefix cache eviction heuristics and tenant-throttling logic failed to protect shared slab resources, leading to multi-tenant degradation and elevated tail latency for host routes. This ticket consolidates post-incident investigation notes, decisions, and an actionable playbook to harden fair-share behavior and rebalance mechanisms to prevent future cross-tenant cascades.

Key findings:
- Burst characteristic: A single tenant issued high-QPS short-lived sequences that evicted large prefix ranges rapidly. The eviction score decay parameters were too aggressive for short-lived bursts, which amplified churn.
- Fairness gap: The fairness controller applied throttles per-connection but lacked integration with the cache admission and rebalance subsystem. As a result, eviction pressure remained unbounded while throttles reduced incoming throughput, causing a feedback loop and long recovery time.
- Telemetry blind spots: We did not have per-tenant eviction-rate metrics exposed in the console dashboards; aggregated slab metrics hid the tenant causing the disruption.
- Safety net missing: No automated emergency rebalance/oom-probe existed to pause aggressive evictions when eviction-rate exceeded configured thresholds.

Primary goals for this ticket:
1) Implement a per-tenant eviction-rate guard and emergency rebalance action that temporarily pins eviction priority away from affected slabs for a cooldown window.
2) Tighten admission & decayed-eviction-score parameters for short bursts while preserving steady-state hit-rate for large tenants.
3) Add tenant-level telemetry and alerting in Console for rapid detection and runbook triggers.
4) Ship a canary rollout with a reversible kill-switch and verify via synthetic burst tests.

Planned work items (owner -> short description):
- Diego Ruiz -> kvcache: add per-tenant eviction_rate counter and eviction-rate anomaly alert rule (metrics + console panel).
- Priya Shah -> controller: wire eviction_rate into fairness controller and implement emergency_rebalance API (pause aggressive eviction for N seconds and reassign rebalance token).
- Jin Park -> runtime: introduce short-burst mode for decay constants (sampling-based switch when tenant QPS > threshold and average prefix churn > X).
- Ops (oncall rotation) -> runbook: add steps to triage tenant-driven cache storms, manual mitigation (temporary tenant pinning, gradual restart), and escalation.
- QA -> test harness: build synthetic tenant-burst test harness and run during canary with 10K synthetic tenants, validate no cross-tenant degradation.

Monitoring & Alerts:
- New metrics: kvcache.tenant.evictions_per_min, kvcache.tenant.eviction_severity, kvcache.rebalance.actions_per_min (added to internal metrics namespace).
- Alerts: P0 alert when any tenant.evictions_per_min > 5000 and slab_global_eviction_rate > 10% for 5m. P1 alert for burst detection at 1000 evictions/min.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy metric and alert definitions to staging and add dashboard panels (2 days).
2) Implement per-tenant counters + console visibility behind feature flag (1 week).
3) Implement emergency_rebalance with config to tune cooldown (2 weeks).
4) Canary in canary-cluster with synthetic load for 48 hours + manual runbook drills.
5) Gradual rollout to production (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with scheduled monitoring windows.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Decay tuning vs. complexity: Whether to use a heuristic sampling approach for short-burst detection (low complexity, small false positives) or a full adaptive controller using rate-of-change signals (higher complexity, more precise). Decision: start with sampling heuristic; revisit after 2-week canary.
- Emergency rebalance aggressiveness: aggressive pauses reduce tail latency quickly but may increase overall miss-rate; conservative pauses reduce collateral impact but slow recovery. Decision: default conservative (3s cooldown) with ability to escalate to 15s via oncall override.

Artifacts & links:
- Postmortem notes (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/kvcache/2025-02-07-burst-postmortem
- Dashboard (internal): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kvcache/tenant-evictions
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kvcache/pull/420 (eviction counters), https://github.com/redwood-inference/controller/pull/231 (emergency_rebalance)
- Runbook draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/kvcache-tenant-burst.md

Acceptance criteria:
- Per-tenant eviction metrics are visible in Console and alert fires in staging under synthetic burst.
- Emergency rebalance API is implemented and tested in canary; can be toggled via feature flag.
- Canary shows no cross-tenant tail-latency regression compared to baseline within 48h.

Longer-term follow-ups (outside scope of this ticket):
- Explore an adaptive controller that balances eviction costs vs latency SLOs using online learning.
- Investigate cache admission policies per-model to avoid large prefix-spanning entries from single tenants hogging slabs.
